chunks: From him (al-Shaykh), from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadala, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission in exchange for a sum) who pays part of his manumission money, then dies, leaving a son by his concubine. He said: If it was stipulated that if he were unable to pay, he would remain a slave, then his son returns as a slave along with the concubine. And if it was not stipulated, his son becomes free, and he returns the remainder of the manumission money to the master, and his son inherits what remains.

key_terms.بَقِيَّة: Remainder: The unpaid portion of the manumission debt.
key_terms.حُرّ: Free: One who is not a slave.
key_terms.رَجَعَ: Returns/Becomes: Indicates the reversion of status or possession.
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: Mukatab: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَة: Manumission contract/debt: The agreed-upon sum for the slave's freedom.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son of a mukatab slave who dies after paying part of his manumission debt?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the inheritance status of a mukatab's son based on the specific contractual stipulation (shart) regarding residual slavery, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the precise terms of manumission contracts. If the condition of reverting to slavery upon default was not explicitly agreed upon, the son is considered free and inherits the remaining debt, highlighting the principle that freedom is the default state unless otherwise contracted. This distinction underscores the juristic focus on protecting the lineage's status through clear contractual intent.
